articleBody:
A kitchen island should improve your workflow, not create traffic jams. Walk through this measurement checklist before ordering cabinets to verify that your kitchen layout can comfortably handle a freestanding island.

- [ ] Single-cook work aisle width — Professional NKBA guidelines recommend at least 42 inches between cabinet faces so doors and drawers open without obstruction.
- [ ] Multi-cook prep aisle width — Aim for 48 inches of clearance between opposite counters if more than one person regularly preps meals together.
- [ ] Surrounding perimeter walkway width — Confirm at least 36 inches of clear walking space around the non-cooking sides of the island.
- [ ] Refrigerator and oven door swings — Measure fully open appliance doors to ensure they do not collide with island cabinets or pinch walkway space.
- [ ] Dishwasher drop-down clearance — Verify at least 30 to 36 inches remains in front of the open dishwasher door so loading is comfortable.
- [ ] Seating overhang depth — Provide 12 to 18 inches of knee space for counter-height stools so guests do not block walkways while seated.
- [ ] Stone overhang support plan — Plan steel plates or corbels for any heavy stone or quartz overhang extending beyond 6 to 8 inches.
- [ ] Finished flooring transitions — Check that base cabinets rest on level, finished subfloors so the island sits plumb and anchors securely.

How to use this checklist:
Measure your room between finished cabinet faces rather than bare drywall before ordering island cabinetry. If clearances feel tight, adjusting island depth or switching to a peninsula might be the better choice.
